result.text:
You came through Riverside. Two houses broke before Riverside dam did. No. 14 Church Lane and the Pells’ house next door are still standing. The wardens’ list has both on it, beside the instruction to mark an empty door with chalk. It had been tested in rain.

Ruth Vey’s kitchen note is brisk: plums in the bowl, eat them; the spare key where everyone knows; bring only the boxes you can carry. Gil Harrow wrote down why the spillway was deferred in 2009 and 2016: the inspectors called the dam satisfactory, the harbour needed dredging, the school roof leaked, and he believed there was time. Three of those were true. I have put the note back beside his letter.

Ruth Vey’s kitchen note is brisk: plums in the bowl, eat them; the spare key where everyone knows; bring only the boxes you can carry. Gil Harrow wrote down why the spillway was deferred in 2009 and 2016: the inspectors called the dam satisfactory, the harbour needed dredging, the school roof leaked, and he believed there was time. Three of those were true. I have put the note back beside his letter.

issues: “St Bride’s notices put tea on until the last train” extends the tea service beyond the record: the notice says the hall stayed open until the last train and the tea urn was on from five; keep those details distinct.
The reflection reads as a summary of documents and events rather than the archivist speaking to you; the run and records support a more personal reflection grounded in these specific details.
“I have never managed one with papers” gives the archivist an unsupported past; remove it or replace it with what Ruth’s note says about bringing only the boxes you can carry.
